lines.en: Esther, we’ve been studying English together for almost a year, and I’ve been thinking about how much we’ve learned.
lines.pt: Esther, estudamos inglês juntas há quase um ano, e tenho pensado em quanto aprendemos.

lines.en: Me too. My manager, who had been doubting my English, said last week that I had made great progress.
lines.pt: Eu também. Minha gerente, que vinha duvidando do meu inglês, disse semana passada que eu tinha feito grande progresso.

lines.en: That is wonderful. My teacher told me not to translate every word, and it has been changing the way I speak.
lines.pt: Que maravilha. Minha professora me disse para não traduzir cada palavra, e isso tem mudado meu jeito de falar.

lines.en: If I hadn’t joined this class, I would have kept avoiding meetings. Now I even lead them.
lines.pt: Se eu não tivesse entrado nesta turma, teria continuado a evitar reuniões. Agora até conduzo.

lines.en: Remember the first time you spoke? You must have been so nervous. Your hands were shaking.
lines.pt: Lembra a primeira vez que você falou? Deve ter ficado muito nervosa. Suas mãos tremiam.

lines.en: I was! Our teacher admitted she had felt the same way when she started, which made me feel better.
lines.pt: Fiquei! Nossa professora admitiu que tinha sentido o mesmo quando começou, o que me fez sentir melhor.

lines.en: Mistakes have been welcomed here from day one. I should have realised sooner that they help us learn.
lines.pt: Erros são bem-vindos aqui desde o primeiro dia. Eu deveria ter percebido antes que eles nos ajudam a aprender.

lines.en: True. My presentation, which I’d been rehearsing for weeks, was praised by the whole department.
lines.pt: Verdade. Minha apresentação, que eu vinha ensaiando havia semanas, foi elogiada pelo departamento inteiro.

lines.en: Brilliant! I’d rather speak with a few mistakes than stay silent. Not everyone who learns a language is brave enough.
lines.pt: Ótimo! Prefiro falar com alguns erros a ficar calada. Nem todo mundo que aprende uma língua é corajoso o bastante.

lines.en: Exactly. The more we practise, the more confident we become, provided that we keep going every week.
lines.pt: Exato. Quanto mais praticamos, mais confiantes ficamos, desde que continuemos toda semana.

lines.en: Then let’s keep going. Whoever sees us now would never believe we were beginners last year.
lines.pt: Então vamos continuar. Quem nos vê agora jamais acreditaria que éramos iniciantes no ano passado.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: I’ve been studying is a present perfect continuous form.
Have been welcomed is a passive form.
We say “If I would have joined”.
items.why: We say If I had joined.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: I’ve been studying is a present perfect continuous form. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Have been welcomed is a passive form. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “If I would have joined”. → Falso (We say If I had joined.)

paragraphs: It is the last class of the term in Houston. Tess and Bia stay behind in the classroom. The board is covered with old notes. They flip through their notebooks together. Each page brings back a memory. Tess smiles and starts the conversation.

“Bia, we’ve been studying English together for almost a year, and I’ve been thinking about how much we’ve learned.” says Tess. “Me too. My manager, who had been doubting my English, said last week that I had made great progress.” says Bia. “That is wonderful. My teacher told me not to translate every word, and it has been changing the way I speak.” says Tess.
